Birendra Prasad Singh And Anr vs The State Of Jharkhand on 5
May, 2016

Author: Rongon Mukhopadhyay
Bench: Rongon Mukhopadhyay
 In The High Court Of Jharkhand At Ranchi

 ----
 1. Birendra Prasad Singh, Son of late K.P. Singh, Resident of 6, Old

 For the Petitioners : Mr. Amit Kumar Das, Advocate
 For the State : Mr. Azeemuddin, App

Heard the parties.

The petitioners in this application have prayed for quashing the entire criminal proceeding in connection with C-2 Case No.512 of 2013 including the order dated 12.02.2013 (12.02.2014), passed by the learned Judicial Magistrate, 1st class, Jamshedpur, whereby and whereunder cognizance has been taken for the offence punishable under section 59 of the Food Safety & Standard Act, 2006 (
hereinafter referred to as the Act)

The allegation made in the prosecution report is to the effect that the Investigating Officer, designated under the Act, had collected sample of "Catch" Haldi (Turmeric) Powder from the store of M/s Steel Workers' Welfare Society as the same did not conform to the Food Safety & Standards Rules, 2011.
On making an analysis, the same was found to be adulterated and unsafe due to presence of 'lead chromate', which is a harmful toxic substance and accordingly prosecution was sought for against the petitioners as well as suppliers and manufacturers.
It has been submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioners that petitioner no. 1 is the Secretary of M/s Steel Workers' Welfare Society and petitioner no. 2 is the Store In-charge.

Learned counsel submits that admittedly the petitioners can be termed to be sellers and in view of section 27 of the Act since none of the conditions are fulfilled so as to prosecute the petitioners, the entire Birendra Prasad Singh And Anr vs The State Of Jharkhand on 5 May, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75353048/
1 proceedings deserves to be quashed and set aside.

sentences.text: Learned counsel has referred to Section 67 of the Act and has submitted that the society of the petitioners also comes within the definition of a Company as per explanation to Section 67 and the society having not been made an accused, the petitioners cannot be made vicariously liable.

Learned A.P.P. has submitted that "Catch" Haldi (Turmeric) Powder was seized from the store of the petitioners and from the report of Food Analyst, it appears that the same does not conform to the prescribed standard of quality specified under the FS&S Regulation-2011 due to presence of lead chromate.

It has been submitted that sanction for launching prosecution had also been given by the Commissioner of Food Safety cum Principal Secretary, Department of Health, Family Welfare and Medical Education, Government of Jharkhand.

sentences.text: Learned APP thus submits that the petitioners can be directly responsible for keeping food products, which does not conform to the prescribed standard and procedure as laid down under the Acts, Rules & Regulations framed thereunder.

In order to appreciate the rival contention, it would be necessary to consider Section 27 of the Act,
which reads as follows:-
27. Liability of Manufacturers, packers, wholesalers, distributors and sellers.-
"(1) The manufacturer or packer of an article of food shall be liable for such article of food if it does not meet the requirements of this Act and the rules and regulations made thereunder.

(2) The wholesaler or distributor shall be liable under this Act for any article of food which is- (a) supplied after the date of its expiry; or (b) stored or supplied in violation of the safety instructions of the manufacturer; or (c) unsafe or misbranded, or (d) unidentifiable of manufacturer from whom the article of food have been received;
or (e) stored or handled or kept in violation of the provisions of this Act, the rules and regulations made thereunder; or (f) received by him with knowledge of being unsafe.

(3) The seller shall be liable under this Act, for any article of food which is- (a) sold after the date of its expiry; or (b) handled or kept in unhygienic conditions; or (c) misbranded; or Birendra Prasad Singh And Anr vs The State Of Jharkhand on 5 May, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75353048/
2 (d) unidentifiable of the manufacturer or the distributors from whom such articles of food were received; or (e) received by him with knowledge of being unsafe".
Section 27 in different parts fixes liability upon manufacturers, packers, wholesalers, distributors and the sellers in facts situation which does not meet the requirement under the Act.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Admittedly,
the petitioners are the Secretary as well as Store Keeper in the Society and thus can be termed as sellers of the product which was seized by the Investigating Officer.
Certain conditions have been enumerated in Sub section (3) of Section 27, by which the seller may be liable for being prosecuted under the Act.

Neither in the prosecution report or in other reports, which have led to the seizure of food product or for that purpose in the counter affidavit, it has been mentioned that any condition as laid down in Sub section (3) of Section 27 is present so to prosecute the sellers.
The Manufacturers or Packers of food article can be made liable if the same does not meet the requirement of the Act, Rules, Regulations framed therein.

In such circumstances, at best the Manufacturers or Packers can be prosecuted and the petitioners being the members of the Society and being sellers cannot be prosecuted in absence of the prosecution in meeting any of the conditions as laid down in Sub Section (3) of Section 27 of the Act.

The other contention, which has been raised by the learned counsel for the petitioners, is with respect to the fact that in absence of the Company having been made an accused the other persons responsible to the Company cannot be made vicariously liable.
Section 67 of the Act deals with the offences by the Companies and in the explanation a Company has been defined to mean any body corporate including a Firm or other association of individuals.
Admittedly, the place, from where the food product was seized was being run by the Steel Workers' Welfare Society, of which the petitioner no. 1 is the Secretary.

The Steel Workers' Welfare Society had never been made an accused and therefore in absence of any specific provision in the Act, the petitioners, who are associated with the Steel Workers' Welfare Society,
could not have been made accused individually and thereby fixing vicarious liablity upon them to face the criminal prosecution in absence of the Society being made an accused.
As a consequence to the discussions made hereinabove, the criminal proceedings, if allowed to continue against the petitioners, shall be an abuse of the process of Court.

Accordingly, this application is allowed and the entire criminal proceedings in connection with C-2 Case No.512 of 2013 including the order dated 12.02.2013 (12.02.2014), passed by the learned Judicial Magistrate, 1st class, Jamshedpur, whereby and whereunder cognizance has been taken for the offence punishable under section 59 of the Food Safety & Standard Act, 2006, are hereby quashed and set aside so far as petitioners are concerned.
(Rongon Mukhopadhyay,J) Rakesh/-
